evidence.quote:
China’s August activity data showed a widening divergence between supply and 
demand, and between manufacturing output and household consumption. Industrial 
production growth accelerated from 4.5% yoy in July to 5.2% in August, while retail sales 
growth slowed from 0.6% yoy to 0.4%. Among major activity indicators, only export 
value and industrial production growth exceeded 5.0% yoy in August. By contrast, many 
domestic demand gauges continued to post large year-over-year declines (Exhibit 1). 
For exports, we can cross-check the data against trading partners’ reported imports 
from China. Such “mirror data” support strong Chinese export growth. For domestic 
demand, however, there are statistical reasons why official data may understate the true 
weakness. For example, in retail sales, large retailers above the designated size are 
surveyed comprehensively, whereas small retailers are sampled and estimated because 
of their large numbers and the difficulty of surveying every small retailer each month 
(see our latest edition of “Understanding China’s Economic Statistics” for more details). 
As a result, officially reported sales growth at small retailers tends to be smoother than 
that at large retailers and to hold up better during economic downturns. In August, sales 
at large retailers declined by almost 4% yoy, while sales at small retailers increased 3% 
yoy (Exhibit 2). This implies an even greater divergence between strong exports and 
weak domestic demand than official data indicate. 
 
The remarkable divergence in the Chinese economy extends beyond exports versus 
domestic demand. Within tech-related manufacturing, for example, industrial robot and 
semiconductor output climbed 34.6% yoy and 20.6% yoy respectively in August, while 
microcomputer and smartphone output dropped 25.6% yoy and 22.3% yoy respectively 
(Exhibit 3). Similarly, within retail sales, communication equipment sales increased 
27.3% yoy in August, while auto sales fell 18.5% yoy (Exhibit 4). These extreme 
divergences, driven in part by the ongoing AI capex boom and policies such as the 
consumer goods trade-in program, make it difficult to characterize the overall strength 
of the Chinese economy.

evidence.quote:
Housing demand weakening again 
After a few months of rising home sales, sales fell 0.7%MoM in August. Stronger 
housing activity over the last few months was one reason for stronger activity in 
Q2. But we have been skeptical that stronger sales reflected a recovery in housing 
demand rather than just usual volatility (we have had similar reservations about 
GDP). In previous years, home sales have tended to decline in winter months and 
rebound sometime in spring or summer. While the pattern is not always the same, 
we suspect this reflects bad seasonal adjustment. 
The trend of home sales also tends to be very sticky month-to-month, suggesting 
some further pullback in sales in coming months. Of course, with upward pressure 
on mortgage rates from higher yields and markets pricing substantial rate hikes 
from the BoC, this would further weigh on housing demand. 
Weaker housing demand should also keep home prices soft. Prices were flat on a 
monthly basis again in August for the third consecutive month but are still lower 
than a year ago. The ratio of home sales to new listings of homes for sale, which 
tends to lead annual home price changes by around 6 months, fell again. We expect  
home prices to continue falling on an annual basis through the rest of this year.

n
widely expected, the meeting was more hawkish than we expected in a few ways.

from our previous expectation that September would be the only hike. We think

deliver hikes that the FOMC presented today as supporting “a timelier return” to 
the 2% target at consecutive meetings. We have kept our forecast for the 
terminal rate unchanged at 3.25-3.5% by adding to the September and 
December 2027 rate cuts we already expected a third 25bp cut in March 2028.

After almost four months of sternly vowing to deliver on price stability, Fed Chair 
Warsh finally went along with the rest of the FOMC in a unanimous decision to 
raise the funds rate 25bp to 3.75-4.0%. The dots delivered a clear message that the 
Committee sees another hike this year as likely appropriate: 16 of 18 who 
submitted projections see at least one more rate hike this year. Moreover, most of 
the Committee sees that rate or higher as appropriate for next year. In his first two 
press conferences, Chair Warsh talked tough about the Fed’s commitment to price 
stability, even as policy was unchanged. Today, his words were similarly hawkish, 
with an “unequivocal” and “unwavering” resolve for price stability. However, this 
time it was delivered against the backdrop of the rate hike, adding to the credence 
of the message from the dot plot. For our part we continue to look for one more hike 
at the December meeting, in line with the revised median FOMC expectations.

evidence.quote:
The FOMC delivered a 25bp rate hike this week. In our base case, cooler 
inflation keeps the Fed on hold in coming months and then leads to cuts 
next year. But risks of further near-term hikes (as early as October) have 
increased as Chair Warsh suggested that there may be more than just a 
“dose of accommodation” to remove and explicitly linked higher energy 
prices to rate increases. Tighter monetary policy will not noticeably slow the 
tailwind to growth from AI-related investment (absent triggering a 
correction in equity markets) but it will push the housing sector deeper into 
contraction, slow non-AI related manufacturing and further reduce already 
low hiring demand. Economic growth will become increasingly dependent 
on just one driver and consequently increasingly fragile.

With only two “dots” indicating no further hikes this year (12 think the Fed should 
hike another 25bp and 4 think 50bp is appropriate) we believe the market is correct 
in assigning significant probability to hikes in October and December. In our base 
case, a cool inflation reading for September, the upcoming election and downward 
revisions to core PCE inflation released September 30th are enough to keep the Fed 
on hold in October awaiting further data. Encouraging inflation data in November 
and December would meet the bar for most Fed officials to again want to hold.

evidence.quote:
The FOMC delivered a 25bp rate hike this week. In our base case, cooler 
inflation keeps the Fed on hold in coming months and then leads to cuts 
next year. But risks of further near-term hikes (as early as October) have 
increased as Chair Warsh suggested that there may be more than just a 
“dose of accommodation” to remove and explicitly linked higher energy 
prices to rate increases. Tighter monetary policy will not noticeably slow the 
tailwind to growth from AI-related investment (absent triggering a 
correction in equity markets) but it will push the housing sector deeper into 
contraction, slow non-AI related manufacturing and further reduce already 
low hiring demand. Economic growth will become increasingly dependent 
on just one driver and consequently increasingly fragile.

With only two “dots” indicating no further hikes this year (12 think the Fed should 
hike another 25bp and 4 think 50bp is appropriate) we believe the market is correct 
in assigning significant probability to hikes in October and December. In our base 
case, a cool inflation reading for September, the upcoming election and downward 
revisions to core PCE inflation released September 30th are enough to keep the Fed 
on hold in October awaiting further data. Encouraging inflation data in November 
and December would meet the bar for most Fed officials to again want to hold.

evidence.quote:
Chair Warsh made the same statement in late August at Jackson Hole, following 
which core CPI registered 0.29%MoM implying a similarly above-target 
0.29%MoM core PCE. But it is not at all how we would read the data over the 
summer. In May, 3m/3m core CPI was 3.1% annualized (and reflected 2x-too-
strong shelter inflation due to the catch-up from missed data collections during 
the October government shutdown). Three months later in August the 3m/3m rate 
declined to 2.0%. 
Core PCE 3m/3m annualized is more elevated but declined from 4.0% to 3.1% over 
the same period. Leaving aside the strong contribution from the rise in equity prices 
and the 10bp boost from wireless phone service prices in August the level looks 
lower and the downtrend more convincing.

evidence.quote:
Energy prices have increased substantially again in recent weeks, causing 
renewed concerns about pass through of higher costs to core inflation. Prices for 
refined products such as diesel in particular present upside risks to goods prices, 
as transportation costs remain higher for longer. 
During last year’s increase in tariffs, we learned that inventories of many retail 
goods could support around 2-3 months of sales. This inventory cycle implied at 
least a few months lag before higher costs resulted in an increase in final selling 
prices. 
Based on the same logic, higher transportation costs beginning six months ago 
should have already boosted the cost of shipping new inventories, and these goods 
would have been sold by now. But so far, the increase in energy prices that began in 
late-February has not clearly resulted in stronger goods prices. Core goods prices in 
CPI have slowed from 1.2%YoY in March to 0.7%YoY as of August. 
Of course, if prices remain elevated or continue to rise, the chance for larger 
increases in final selling prices could grow. But we are cautious to include this 
expectation in our medium-term forecasts.

evidence.quote:
After almost four months of sternly vowing to deliver on price stability, Fed Chair 
Warsh finally went along with the rest of the FOMC in a unanimous decision to 
raise the funds rate 25bp to 3.75-4.0%. The dots delivered a clear message that the 
Committee sees another hike this year as likely appropriate: 16 of 18 who 
submitted projections see at least one more rate hike this year. Moreover, most of 
the Committee sees that rate or higher as appropriate for next year. In his first two 
press conferences, Chair Warsh talked tough about the Fed’s commitment to price 
stability, even as policy was unchanged. Today, his words were similarly hawkish, 
with an “unequivocal” and “unwavering” resolve for price stability. However, this 
time it was delivered against the backdrop of the rate hike, adding to the credence 
of the message from the dot plot. For our part we continue to look for one more hike 
at the December meeting, in line with the revised median FOMC expectations.

houses.summary: GS 최신 글로벌 정책표는 미국의 다음 25bp 인상을 12월로 적고 이후 2027년 50bp 인하를 제시했다.
houses.comment: AI 비교: 앞서 저장된 GS 10월 인상 전망과 시점이 다르므로 최신 자료의 12월 표기를 우선하되 변경의 상세 사유는 미확인이다.
houses.limitation: 표지 9월 20일 18:45 EDT·메타데이터 9월 21일. 글로벌 추적 보고서의 후속 정책 경로이며 FOMC 결정의 확정 지침이 아니다. 미국 전용 후속 원문과 재대조 필요.

the US (another +25bp in December followed by 
-50bp of cuts in 2027).

houses.summary: Citi는 만장일치 인상이 이후 긴축 강도에 대한 완전한 합의를 뜻하지 않으며 일부 위원이 물가 둔화를 더 긍정적으로 볼 수 있다고 분석했다. Williams 등의 발언을 확인 대상으로 제시했다.
houses.comment: AI 비교: 실제 표결과 향후 경로의 이견 가능성을 구분하며 아직 나오지 않은 발언을 사실로 쓰지 않는다.

evidence.quote:
We are most interested in what NY Fed President Williams has to say after as late as 
just prior to the release of CPI he described policy rates as "in a good place."  While 
agreeing to raise rates at last week's FOMC meeting, Williams might still be of the 
view that policy rates are close to where they should be, which would be a 
significantly less hawkish characterization than when Chair Warsh indicated the 
FOMC had merely removed a "dose of accommodation."
Chair Warsh presented the committee as unanimous in its resolve to lower 
inflation. But we expect some policymakers will have interpreted recent data as 
more encouraging for disinflation, suggesting less impetus for further rate hikes.

event_reviews.headline: FOMC 후속: GS 최신 표는 12월, Citi는 이견 주목
event_reviews.summary: 정책금리 범위 3.75~4.00%는 원본 예상에 부합한 25bp 인상이다. AI 비교: GS 최신 글로벌 보고서는 앞선 10월과 달리 다음 인상을 12월로 적었다. JPM의 12월 전망과 시점이 같아졌으나 GS 변경 사유는 미국 전용 후속 보고서 확인이 필요하다. Citi는 표결 만장일치와 추가 인상 동의는 다를 수 있다고 본다.
event_reviews.watch: Fed 위원 발언과 GS 미국 전용 정책경로의 날짜·시점을 재대조한다.

houses.summary: JPM의 9월 16일 FOMC 사후 분석은 25bp 인상과 추가 인상을 시사한 점도표를 강조하며 12월 한 차례 추가 인상 전망을 유지했다.
houses.comment: AI 비교: Citi의 회의 전 연내 추가 동결 전망과 다르지만 동일 시점의 사후 견해 비교는 아니다. 회의 이후 Citi의 후속 평가는 미확보다.
houses.limitation: 동일 Sep 16 회의의 사후 보고서다. 원본 달력은 9월 17일 03:00, 보고서는 미국 9월 16일로 날짜가 달라 기존 날짜 검증상 관련 분석으로 보수적으로 분류했다. 시간대는 원본에 명시되지 않아 변환하지 않았으며 사전 전망으로 취급하지 않는다.

evidence.quote:
After almost four months of sternly vowing to deliver on price stability, Fed Chair 
Warsh finally went along with the rest of the FOMC in a unanimous decision to 
raise the funds rate 25bp to 3.75-4.0%. The dots delivered a clear message that the 
Committee sees another hike this year as likely appropriate: 16 of 18 who 
submitted projections see at least one more rate hike this year. Moreover, most of 
the Committee sees that rate or higher as appropriate for next year. In his first two 
press conferences, Chair Warsh talked tough about the Fed’s commitment to price 
stability, even as policy was unchanged. Today, his words were similarly hawkish, 
with an “unequivocal” and “unwavering” resolve for price stability. However, this 
time it was delivered against the backdrop of the rate hike, adding to the credence 
of the message from the dot plot. For our part we continue to look for one more hike 
at the December meeting, in line with the revised median FOMC expectations.

evidence.quote:
The final eurozone inflation print for August was 3.2% y-o-y, 0.1ppt lower than the 
flash release. This marked a 0.3ppt rise from July’s rate of 2.9% y-o-y. The revision 
reflected a fall in the monthly inflation rate in services (from 0.1% m-o-m to flat), 
though core HICP inflation was unchanged from the flash print at 2.4% y-o-y (down 
from 2.5% a month earlier).

houses.comment: AI 비교: 근원 둔화와 전체 물가 재상승 위험을 분리한다.
houses.limitation: GS 원문 전체 전년비 3.25%와 WECO 3.2%의 표시 정밀도가 다르다. 원본 수치는 변경하지 않는다.

evidence.quote:
Our summary indicator of 
sequential underlying inflation declined by another 1bp in August but still stands at a 
relatively elevated rate of 0.22%mom. The change in our sequential summary 
measure reflects a sequential decline across most of the metrics we track, with the 
biggest moves recorded in the persistence-weighted (+0.10pp), supercore (-0.07pp), 
and HICPXX (-0.06pp) measures. Updating our medium-term inflation infrastructure 
with the final details and another month of the underlying summary measure, our 
medium-term path continues to show core inflation at a strong 2.4%yoy in 2026, 
peaking at 2.7%yoy in 2027Q1 before gradually declining to 2.0%yoy in 2028Q4. As 
for headline inflation, incorporating the final details for the fuels components and 
the two weeks of higher-frequency pump price data for September, we now see the 
peak at 3.8%yoy in 2026Q4 (up from 3.6%yoy previously), as we upgrade the energy 
component by 2pp to 18%yoy for Q4.

houses.summary: JPM은 단독주택 반등에도 허가가 연초 대비 5.9% 낮아 주택 둔화가 해소됐다는 증거가 부족하고 3분기 실질 주거투자의 소폭 감소에 부합한다고 봤다.
houses.comment: AI 비교: GS의 이번 GDP 추적치 상향과 JPM의 주거투자 수준 전망은 서로 다른 비교 기준이다.

evidence.quote:
The August housing starts report provided little evidence that the broader housing 
slowdown is easing. While activity in the key single-family segment rebounded 
modestly after a midyear slowdown, forward-looking indicators continue to point 
to soft construction activity ahead. Single-family starts rose 7.6%m/m to 918k saar, 
and the July figure was revised higher. Even so, starts remain 3.0% below their 
level at the start of the year. Total starts fell 2.6%m/m to 1.275mn saar as the volatile 
multifamily segment declined 21.7%. More concerning, building permits, a 
leading indicator of future construction activity, fell 2.7%m/m in August and 
remain 5.9% below their level at the start of the year. The decline in permits was 
broad-based, with both single-family (-1.8%) and multifamily authorizations 
moving lower. Today’s report remains consistent with our expectation for a modest 
contraction in real residential investment in 3Q.

houses.summary: Citi는 높은 금리와 수요 약화가 착공·허가를 추가로 낮추고 주거투자가 향후 GDP에 부담을 줄 것으로 봤다.
houses.comment: AI 비교: 단독주택의 한 달 반등을 추세 회복으로 보지 않는다는 점에서 JPM과 유사하다.

evidence.quote:
Data – Housing starts fell for a second month in August, falling to 1275k. Single 
family housing starts rebounded to 918k while multifamily starts fell to 357k. 
Building permits also declined in August, falling to 1394k. Single family building 
permits fell to 878k while multifamily permits fell to 516k. 
Citi’s view – Housing starts have softened in recent months and will likely pull back 
further as higher rates weigh on housing demand. Recent high frequency data have 
already showed a renewed slowing in housing activity, with mortgage applications 
now falling on an annual basis for the first time since late 2024. We expect 
residential investment to continue to weigh on GDP growth in coming quarters.

evidence.quote:
4. Initial jobless claims decreased by 10k to 196k in the week ended September 12, 
below consensus expectations. The four-week moving average of claims decreased by 
3k to 203k. Claims rose by 2k in Ohio and Kentucky and declined by 3k in Michigan and

persons receiving benefits through standard programs—decreased by 39k to 1,730k in

January 2024.

houses.summary: JPM은 최근 몇 년보다 낮은 청구가 고용 증가와 실업률 하락에 부합한다고 봤다. 노동절·잔존 계절성을 지적하고 계속청구가 9월 하순 다시 오를 가능성을 열어뒀다.
houses.comment: AI 비교: 청구 감소를 신규 채용 급증으로 동일시하지 않는다.

evidence.quote:
Jobless claims continue to run well below recent years, a positive indicator for job 
growth and consistent with gradually lower unemployment. Initial claims in the 
week ending September 12 fell 10k to 196k, near the lows for this year. The week 
included the Labor Day holiday and there could be some seasonal noise. Residual 
seasonality unrelated to the Labor Day holiday also has left claims tending to drift 
lower in the fall and winter. In any case the basic story of initial claims running 
below the last few years remains intact. Meanwhile, continuing claims in the week 
ending September 5 fell 39k to 1.730mn, a new low for this year. Continuing claims 
are at similar levels to May 2023, a time when the unemployment rate was only 
3.6%. The pattern of residual seasonality in continuing claims is different than for 
initial claims, and continuing claims could edge higher again starting in late 
September.

evidence.quote:
1. The Philadelphia Fed manufacturing index decreased (-9.6pt to 37.8) in September, 
above expectations for a larger decline, after reaching in August its highest level since 
April 2021. The composition of the report was soft, with declines in the employment 
(-16.1pt to 11.8) and new orders (-0.9pt to 29.2) components and an unchanged 
reading for the shipments component at 27.7.  Both the prices paid (+7.7pt to +48.6) 
and the prices received (+13.6pt to +31.3) measures increased. The delivery times 
component increased by 22.8pt to 26.5, indicating that delivery times increased on net. 
This marks the highest level in the delivery times component since March 2022, 
consistent with similar increases in delivery times observed across other business 
surveys. The 6 months-ahead business conditions index declined by 20.7pt to +52.9, 
after reaching in August its highest level since 1983.

evidence.quote:
Pending home sales, which typically lead existing home sales by one to two 
months, edged up 0.3%m/m in August. However, July’s decline was revised more 
negative, leaving contract signings down 7.0% over the past three months, a period 
during which the average 30-year fixed mortgage rate rose roughly 25bp. The NAR 
index remains near a six-month low and continues to run well below historical 
norms. Regionally, gains in the South (+2.3%m/m) and West (+3.0%) were offset 
by declines in the Northeast (-4.2%) and Midwest (-1.6%). All four regions posted 
year-ago declines.

evidence.quote:
Korea’s producer price index (PPI) rose 7.9% oya in August, picking up slightly 
after a gradual moderation over the previous three months. On our seasonally 
adjusted basis, the headline PPI nearly reversed July’s dip, rising 0.4% m/m sa. The 
monthly result was broad-based, except for flat food prices, with energy PPI 
rebounding. In a broader context, PPI trend inflation decelerated to 6.0% 3m/3m 
saar, moving closer to the pre-conflict pace seen earlier this year. Today’s readings 
suggest that sequential PPI disinflation may still be in the pipeline, yet the path is 
likely to remain volatile given ongoing geopolitical risks.

houses.summary: JPM은 신선식품 제외 CPI 1.7% 둔화가 전기·가스 보조금과 쌀값 하락의 영향을 받았고, 식품·에너지 제외 지수는 계절조정 전월비 0.3% 올라 기조 압력이 남았다고 봤다.
houses.comment: AI 비교: 신선식품 제외와 전체 식품·에너지 제외 지수는 정의가 다르므로 같은 근원 수치로 비교하지 않는다.

evidence.quote:
The August nationwide CPI came out weaker than expected, with the core measure 
(ex. fresh food) rising just 0.1%m/m sa to 1.7%oya, a notch softer than 1.8% in the 
previous month. That said, the main drivers of the slowdown were the 
government’s resumption of electricity and gas subsidies and a deceleration in food 
inflation stemming from falling rice prices. Meanwhile, the core (ex. food and 
energy) measure that better captures underlying inflation continued to rise by 
0.3%m/m sa in August, as in the prior month, bringing the oya rate to 1.6%. Various 
government “cost-of-living measures” are still suppressing inflation across a wide 
range of categories—including gasoline, electricity and gas, high school tuition, 
and school lunch fees—thereby pushing down the headline inflation rate. 
However, supported by firm domestic demand, the pass-through of higher 
petroleum product prices and wage costs into consumer prices appears to be 
gaining momentum.

houses.summary: Citi는 보조금·쌀값으로 근원이 1.7%로 낮아졌으나 유가 전가로 9월 2%를 넘고 내년 초 3%에 접근할 것으로 예상했다. BOJ 예상 범위 안이어서 정책 영향은 제한적이라고 봤다.
houses.comment: AI 비교: JPM과 일시적 하락 요인에는 동의하되 Citi는 이번 발표 자체의 정책 파급을 제한적으로 평가한다.

evidence.quote:
The August nationwide core CPI (ex-fresh food) rose 1.7% YoY, down from 
+1.8% YoY in July and undershooting the market consensus. Food inflation 
continued to moderate amid declining rice prices, and energy’s contribution 
turned negative as the government reintroduced electricity and gas 
subsidies. These developments pushed core CPI down. Going forward, 
however, we expect higher oil prices due to the escalation of the Middle East 
situation to feed through to CPI with a lag, and core CPI looks likely to rise 
towards 3% again into early next year. While government subsidies are 
expected to offset the impact of rising oil prices to some extent during 
August-October, we expect core CPI to rise above 2% again in September, 
followed by a further acceleration from November and beyond. That said, 
this is well within the BoJ’s range of assumptions and thus should have a 
limited monetary policy impact, in our view.

houses.summary: HSBC는 전체 CPI 1.9%, 신선식품 제외 1.7%를 확인했다.
houses.comment: AI 비교: 전체와 근원을 구분하며 두 수치 모두 원본과 일치한다.

event_reviews.headline: BOJ 1.25% 인상, 다음 시점은 IB별 차이
event_reviews.summary: BOJ는 예상대로 1.00%에서 1.25%로 25bp 올렸다. AI 비교: JPM·Citi는 12월 추가 인상, HSBC는 2027년 1분기 기본, GS 최신 글로벌 표는 2026년 말 1.25%를 제시한다. 전망과 위험 시나리오를 구분한다.
event_reviews.watch: 엔화·Fed 경로, 보조금 제외 물가와 BOJ 금융여건 평가를 확인한다.

houses.summary: GS 정책 추적 보고서는 일본 정책금리를 2026년 말 1.25%, 2027년 말 1.75%로 제시했다.
houses.comment: AI 비교: 올해 말 수준 유지 전망은 JPM·Citi의 12월 추가 인상과 다르다.
houses.limitation: 표지 9월 20일 18:45 EDT·메타데이터 9월 21일. 9월 18일 BOJ 이후의 글로벌 정책 경로 보고서이며 결정문 자체가 아니다.

evidence.quote:
We also revised up our forecasts in 
Australia (+25bp to 4.6% in 2026, +50bp to 4.1% in 2027) and Japan (+25bp in 
both years, to 1.25% and 1.75%).

houses.summary: JPM은 향후 물가 상승 경로를 근거로 다음 BOJ 인상을 12월로 유지했다.
houses.comment: AI 비교: HSBC의 2027년 1분기보다 이른 경로다.

evidence.quote:
We continue to expect the BoJ’s next rate hike to come in December, as inflation is likely to 
remain on an upward trend in coming quarters.

houses.summary: Citi는 두 명의 반대가 내년 이사회 구성 변화 전 인상을 서두를 유인을 높인다고 해석해 2026년 12월, 2027년 3월·7월 인상을 기본으로 제시했다.
houses.comment: AI 비교: 반대 표를 단순 비둘기 신호로만 읽지 않는 해석이며 BOJ의 확정 일정이 아니다.

evidence.quote:
The BoJ raised its policy rate from 1.00% to 1.25% today, as widely expected. 
The voting behavior was our biggest focus, and this saw Board Members 
Asada and Sato cast dissenting votes against the rate hike. While this raises 
the hurdle for continued rate hikes after the retirement of hawkish members 
in July next year, we think it also paradoxically increases the likelihood of a 
faster pace to the terminal rate. The future path of rate hikes will depend 
significantly on Fed policy, but given that the Fed raised rates this week—
contrary to our previous house view—the probability of an additional BoJ 
rate hike within the year, rather than in January, has increased. Looking 
beyond that, it would be prudent to complete rate hikes while hawkish 
members remain on the board, and we now expect hikes in December 2026 
and March and July 2027 as our base scenario.

houses.summary: HSBC는 2027년 1분기 25bp 추가 인상으로 1.50%를 기본 전망으로 유지하되 Fed의 추가 인상으로 12월 BOJ 인상 가능성이 커질 위험을 제시했다.
houses.comment: AI 비교: JPM·Citi의 12월 기본과 HSBC의 12월 위험 시나리오를 구분한다.
houses.limitation: 1쪽의 vote to hold 표현은 같은 페이지 사실·2쪽의 7대2 인상 설명과 충돌한다. 결정은 WECO와 명확한 2쪽 설명을 기준으로 확인했다.

evidence.quote:
We therefore maintain our baseline view that the BoJ will pause until the first quarter of 2027, when we expect a further 
25bp hike to lift the policy rate to 1.50%. 
Looking ahead, we also think the US Federal Reserve and Japan’s fiscal policies will weigh heavily on BoJ moves. 
The Fed’s increasingly hawkish stance puts pressure on the BoJ and other Asian central banks to tighten policy, particularly those 
facing currency weakness. Since the Fed raised rates earlier this week, the BoJ’s decision today merely kept pace and did not 
narrow the interest-rate differential. HSBC US economist Ryan Wang expects the Fed to deliver one further 25bp hike on 9 
December, which poses a risk to our baseline view by increasing the likelihood of a BoJ hike at its 18 December MPM

evidence.quote:
A run of solid gains in manufacturing activity took a breather in August, with 
factory output pulling back 0.3% on the month and posting its first outright decline 
since December 2025. Total industrial production was unchanged, as a 1.8% 
increase in utilities output offset the decline in manufacturing. Taken together, the 
July and August data leave manufacturing output tracking a modest 0.7%q/q, saar 
gain in 3Q, with total IP up 1.7%. While that would represent a notable downshift 
from 2Q, when manufacturing and total IP expanded at annualized rates of 5.2% 
and 4.2%, respectively, early September regional manufacturing surveys still point 
to solid activity in the months ahead, though elevated prices and longer delivery 
times suggest supply-side and inflation pressures remain a concern.
